text: Chebyshev approximation Chebyshev approximation uses endpoint-clustered nodes and a connection with trigonometric functions. Interpolation, weighted projection and best uniform approximation are distinct constructions. Problem and representative equations Set Tₖ(cosθ)=cos(kθ) and approximate f on [−1,1] by ΣaₖTₖ. Lobatto nodes xⱼ=cos(jπ/n) allow interpolation coefficients to be computed by a discrete cosine transform. Orthogonality uses weight (1−x²)⁻¹/², not the unit weight of Legendre polynomials. T0(x)=1,T1(x)=x,Tk+1(x)=2xTk(x)−Tk−1(x),xj=cos⁡(jπ/n).T0​(x)=1,T1​(x)=x,Tk+1​(x)=2xTk​(x)−Tk−1​(x),xj​=cos(jπ/n). Algorithm Map the physical interval, sample the nodes, compute coefficients and evaluate the series by recurrence. Clenshaw–Curtis quadrature integrates the interpolant; its nodes and exactness properties are not identical to Gaussian quadrature. Conditions and pitfalls Analytic functions can give rapid coefficient decay, while jumps cause Gibbs oscillations and finite smoothness slows decay. Differentiation amplifies coefficient errors. A small coefficient tail alone cannot rule out unresolved features between sampling nodes. What to check Test reproduction of Tₖ, nodal interpolation and approximation of exp(x), then compare convergence for an absolute value or jump. Measure errors off the interpolation grid and verify derivative scaling under interval maps.
